item.content:encoded:
Doing silly things in a party is one thing, doing silly things in a serious situation is another. For me, asking to be killed by an SCP item to end your life is actually a serious situation.

Professional people don't have to be serious all the time, but I've seen many, many Foundation personnel acting in a joker or silly manner when they should've acted seriously. It brokes my suspensión of disbelief. Is like if everybody is Groucho Marx.

And, yesterday, I saw it again in this page. My complain was about it, not because the Foundation staff doesn't act like robots.

English isn't my main language, I'm sorry if I've said something wrong.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I work in a serious, and professional organization. We run the world's largest bond trading platform in the world. A second's lapse in attention could mean millions in damages.

Everything is high risk, and super critical, and we're constantly on call.

We also had a beach party a few days ago, where we all wore hawaiian shirts, and played limbo, acting like fools.

Serious people are not serious all the time. These are people. Not robots.

I mean, I am now, thanks to this tale. And I think it's hilarious, because it's absurd and absurdity can be very funny.

I mean, if you don't find the concept funny, that's cool. But your reasoning for it makes me feel like you wouldn't find anything funny, ever.

Hmmmm… Maybe I've a heart of Stone, but I didn't laugh. As the joke was the center of the article, I don't have any reasons to upvote.
Also, there's something about this tale that annoys me; is its no serious and excessively joker undertone, wich is almost a cliche within the tales. Do you have the sensation that nearly every doctor of the Foundation likes joking and acts in a no-serious manner even in situations that are completely serious? I do.
Huh, the last thing I'd like to do in my life is to make 173 slide in a banana peel. Do you imagine a person in the real life acting like this? Do you imagine dozens of persons in a serious and professional organization acting like this? I don't. And I've seen this kind of thing too many times; I think it's hackneyed.

I know some people may disagree with my reasons, but my vote is -1.

god-tier shitpost

this is a great example of how shifting tones can really amplify a joke's final bang. you present a dark, melodramatic opening with a prevalent theme of death and moving on and accepting the inevitable, while not ignoring the intended end result. we get hints at that box, vague intimations of something crazy, and then we get the banana revelation, which is then made whole by 173 breaking character and hwooping his ass, or more accurately his face-ass. fass.

in short it's great comedy and i loooove it. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bqr1QKLb-rM
